findings.title: Tier 2 NFR is restated with specific targets and the gate exceeds it
findings.description: The design restates the architecture's Tier 2 target (60 TPS at N=50k on CUDA) and sets A3 at ≥ 100 TPS (1.67× headroom) plus A2 at ≥ 5× on `force_total`, matching the slice-plan entry for (149) exactly (≥5× force_total, ≥100 TPS, 20% statistical parity). No ambiguity about which host measures what (A1/A4 Mac, A2/A3/A5 CUDA).

findings.title: Correct architectural boundaries; seam and downstream interface preserved
findings.description: The fused tick legitimately operates outside `SpatialQuery`/`BulkForce` per the architecture's explicit exception principle. The design keeps `get_neighbors_first_k` as the documented A7 swap point (Option A), changes no `TickResult`/world-server surface, and correctly identifies that slice 146 stays unblocked. The `break`-in-caller placement is technically correct for Quadrants: a `@qd.func` cannot break the enclosing kernel loop, so the guard-then-break structure is the right mechanism (consistent with the slice 145 Phase 2 POC finding that `break` compiles in an inner range loop).

findings.title: Config validation fails explicitly; subdivision coverage math is sound
findings.description: `S` is validated at config-load time with hard `ValueError`s (non-integer, < 1, > 8) — no silent clamp, per project policy. The (2S+1)×(2S+1) scan with `cell_size = query_radius / S` provably covers the same physical radius (worst-case agent-at-cell-edge leaves ≥ S·cell_size margin on each axis), and `S=1` reproduces slice 145's loop bounds exactly.

findings.title: Config mechanism for S/cell_size doesn't match the actual bench harness
findings.description: The design names three inconsistent mechanisms, none of which matches the code: (1) "BenchConfig" — no such component exists; the harness config surface is the `Workload` YAML loader (`src/migratory/bench/workload.py`), which has a strict required-field schema and no `subdivision_factor` field today (unknown keys are silently ignored, so adding one to YAML without loader changes would do nothing). (2) The walkthrough commands (`scripts/bench.py --config mid-flock-50k --subdivision-factor 3 --ticks 200 --parity-check numpy`) reference a CLI that doesn't exist — the real entry point is `python -m migratory.bench` with `--workload`/`--backend` only (`src/migratory/bench/cli.py:23-34`); there is no `--ticks` or `--parity-check` flag, and tick counts come from the workload YAML. (3) The claim "the bench harness passes cell_size at setup; it reads from config" is inaccurate: `GpuAgentState.setup()` computes `cell_size = max_query_radius * DEFAULT_CELL_SIZE_MULTIPLIER` internally (`src/migratory/bench/backends/quadrants_fused_state.py:150`) — it is not passed in. The design should name the real seam (e.g., a `subdivision_factor` field on `Workload` threaded through `GpuAgentState.setup()` as `max_query_radius / S`, replacing the hardcoded multiplier) and state whether `--subdivision-factor` is a new CLI override or a workload-YAML field. "Refined after implementation" does not cover this: the loader/backends touched (runner vs state) determine where the validation code lives.

findings.title: Gate workload `mid-flock-50k` resolves to N=100,000, contradicting the design's N=50k premise
findings.description: The design's gate configuration is "mid-flock-50k workload, S=3, max_neighbors=32" with A2/A3 measured at N=50k. The checked-in `bench/workloads/mid-flock-50k.yaml` has `n: 100000` while its own description says "N=50k operating point" (and its `cluster_centers` at [120,120]/[280,280] with radius 45 look scaled for a 400×400 world, not 1536×1536). Since `GpuAgentState.setup()` reads `workload.n` directly, A2/A3 as written would be measured at N=100k against a slice-145 baseline recorded at N=50k — invalidating the ≥5× and ≥100 TPS comparisons. The slice design should either call out the workload correction as in-scope or pin the exact workload definition (N, world size, cluster geometry) the gates run against; the p99-occupancy premise (~5000/cell) the entire speedup model rests on was measured under a specific formation config.

findings.title: Walkthrough Step 3 cannot reproduce the baseline with the shown commands
findings.description: The "Baseline (S=1, counter-gating)" and "Early exit only (S=1, break enabled)" commands are byte-identical; once the break is merged there is no flag that disables it, so the baseline must come from the recorded slice-145 numbers (force_total ≈ 25.18 ms at N=50k) or from a temporary disable mechanism. A2 permits using recorded numbers, but the walkthrough should say so explicitly rather than implying a fresh same-command baseline run.

structured_findings.summary: Tier 2 NFR is restated with specific targets and the gate exceeds it
Correct architectural boundaries; seam and downstream interface preserved
Config validation fails explicitly; subdivision coverage math is sound
Config mechanism for S/cell_size doesn't match the actual bench harness
Gate workload `mid-flock-50k` resolves to N=100,000, contradicting the design's N=50k premise
Walkthrough Step 3 cannot reproduce the baseline with the shown commands
